themes: Operating leverage in exchanges and brokers
key_points: Monthly SIP flows reached Rs310bn in May 2026, up 48% YoY, despite Nifty 50 delivering only 0.8% CAGR over 2 years in rupee terms
FPIs sold $36bn of Indian equities in FY25-26, yet cumulative equity and balanced fund net inflows were Rs9.43tn, validating structural retail participation
Exchange ADPTV surged from Rs10bn in FY14 to Rs699bn in FY26, driven by index options and weekly expiry proliferation
Preferred stock selection: AngelOne > CAMS > ICICIAMC > NAM > HDFCAMC based on pricing power, regulatory resilience, competitive intensity, cyclicality, operating leverage, and valuation
AngelOne offers best growth-adjusted valuation with FY26-28E EPS CAGR of 36% and PEG of 0.7x despite cheapest multiple at 19.8x FY28E P/E
Tax policy supportive: 12.5% LTCG on equity versus slab-rate taxation on debt mutual funds improves relative appeal
Key risks to thesis: SIP inflows falling below Rs250bn sustained period or regulatory action reducing derivative volumes by >20%
catalysts: Monthly SIP flows sustaining above Rs300bn
Market share gains by capital markets participants
Regulatory clarity on derivatives volumes and weekly expiries
reports.summary: India's capital markets sector is structurally driven by SIP-led financialization, with monthly SIP flows at Rs310bn despite weak equity returns, supporting capital markets infrastructure beneficiaries. JPMorgan initiates sector coverage with bullish ratings on brokers (AngelOne), RTAs (CAMS), and AMCs (ICICIAMC, NAM, HDFCAMC), while remaining cautious on depositories (CDSL) and commodities (MCX) where valuations have already priced in strength. The investment thesis hinges on persistent SIP inflows above Rs250bn and regulatory support for derivatives markets.
reports.connection_narrative: India's capital market financialization story is driven by three structural forces: first, tax policy favoring equity with 12.5% long-term capital gains taxation versus slab-rate taxation on debt mutual funds; second, behavioral momentum from set-and-forget retail SIP participation that has proven resilient through volatility despite weak headline equity returns; and third, policy support maintaining equity market accessibility through derivatives and broking innovation. These macro drivers are creating durable demand for capital market infrastructure regardless of near-term equity market performance. AngelOne, JPMorgan's top pick, is optimally positioned because it combines the low-cost broker model with highest operating leverage in the sector—as retail SIP flows scale, their fixed-cost base generates accelerating earnings while pricing discipline compounds margins, reflected in the best-in-class PEG of 0.7x with 36% EPS growth. CAMS benefits as the dominant MF RTA with 68% market share, capturing 76% of equity net sales and 65% of SIP registrations while expanding into higher-margin non-MF businesses. Among asset managers, ICICIAMC stands apart with 83-86% RoE and market-leading equity inflows despite TER regulation capping operating leverage, validating its franchise quality where faster SIP growth translates directly to earnings. The exchanges BSE and MCX have both re-rated sharply on derivatives momentum—BSE's index options segment growing 104% YoY and MCX's bullion ADT surging 496% on geopolitical supply disruptions—but JPMorgan counsels caution as these moves appear cyclically driven by elevated volatility that may not persist. The single most important catalyst to watch is whether monthly SIP flows can sustain above Rs300bn through a potential market downturn, as this determines whether the financialization thesis remains intact; conversely, the key risk is regulatory action restricting retail derivatives participation or weekly expiry products, which could reduce ADPTV volumes by 20% and invalidate exchange valuations.
